fields.symptoms: The patient presented with a persistent cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, mild fever, fatigue, and occasional headaches for the past four days. Vital signs were stable, and no signs of severe respiratory distress were observed during the examination.
fields.treatment: Prescribed a 5-day course of antibiotics based on clinical assessment, along with paracetamol for fever and pain relief. Advised the patient to maintain adequate hydration, get sufficient rest, and perform warm saltwater gargles to relieve throat discomfort. The patient was instructed to return for a follow up visit in one week or immediately if symptoms worsen, including high fever, difficulty breathing, or persistent chest pain.

fields.symptoms: The patient presented with abdominal cramps, frequent watery stools, nausea, and two episodes of vomiting over the past 24 hours. He also reported mild dizziness and weakness due to reduced fluid intake. Physical examination showed mild signs of dehydration, while vital signs remained stable.
fields.treatment: The patient was advised to begin oral rehydration therapy immediately to replace lost fluids and electrolytes. Medications were prescribed to relieve nausea and abdominal discomfort. He was instructed to maintain a light diet, avoid spicy and oily foods, increase fluid intake, and monitor for any worsening symptoms such as persistent vomiting, high fever, or blood in the stool. A follow-up appointment was scheduled in three days to assess recovery.

fields.treatment: The patient was started on antihypertensive medication and advised to monitor blood pressure regularly. fields.symptoms: The patient presented with a persistent cough, sore throat, mild fever, painful swallowing, fatigue, and swollen cervical lymph nodes. Symptoms have persisted for several days despite the use of over-the-counter medication. Physical examination revealed redness and inflammation of the throat without signs of respiratory distress. fields.treatment: The patient was prescribed an appropriate antibiotic regimen to treat the bacterial infection, along with analgesics for pain and fever relief. He was advised to maintain adequate hydration, rest, perform warm saltwater gargles three to four times daily, and avoid cold drinks and irritants such as cigarette smoke. A follow-up appointment was scheduled in one week to assess recovery. The patient was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms worsen or if difficulty breathing or swallowing develops.
